ee:2014:q2.title: GATE EE 2014 | Set 1 | Question: 2
ee:2014:q2.question: Let $f(x)=xe^{-x}$. The maximum value of the function in the interval $(0,\infty )$ is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} f(x)&=xe^{-x}\\ f'(x)&=e^{-x}-xe^{-x}=0\\ e^{-x}(1-x)&=0\\ x&=1\\ f''(x)&=-e^{-x}-e^{-x}+xe^{-x}\\ &=e^{-x}(x-2)\\ f''(1)&=e^{-1}(-1)=-e^{-1} \lt 0 \end{aligned}$$

Hence f(x) has maximum value at x=1

$f(1)=1\cdot e^{-1}=e^{-1}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ee:2014:q7.question: $C_0$ is the capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor with air as dielectric (as in figure (a)). If, half of the entire gap as shown in figure (b) is filled with a dielectric of permittivity $\epsilon _r$ , the expression for the modified capacitance is

detailed_solution.markdown: Let A be the area of the parallel plate capacitor and d be the distance between the plates. Let $C_1$ be the capacitance of half portion with air as dielectic medium and $C_2$ be capacitance with a dielectic of permitivity, $\varepsilon _r$. ee:2014:q36.title: GATE EE 2014 | Set 1 | Question: 36
ee:2014:q36.question: The core loss of a single phase, 230/115 V, 50 Hz power transformer is measured from 230 V side by feeding the primary (230 V side) from a variable voltage variable frequency source while keeping the secondary open circuited. The core loss is measured to be 1050 W for 230 V, 50 Hz input. The core loss is again measured to be 500 W for 138 V, 30 Hz input. The hysteresis and eddy current losses of the transformer for 230 V, 50 Hz input are respectively,

detailed_solution.markdown:
Given, at 230V, 50 Hz, core loss =1050 W

and at 138 V, 30 Hz, core loss =500 W

Let, $V_1=230 V, \;f_1=50Hz$

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Eddy current loss} &=P_{e1} \\ \text{Hysteresis loss}&=P_{h1} \\ V_2=138V &, f_230Hz \\ \text{Eddy current loss} &=P_{e2} \\ \text{Hysteresis loss}&=P_{h2} \\ \text{we know that, } & \\ \text{Eddy current loss,}\;& P_e \propto B_m^2f^2 \\ \text{and hysteresis loss,}&P_h \propto B_m^xf\propto B_m^1.6 f \\ &(\text{Typical value of x=1.6}) \end{aligned}$$

The transformer induced emf equation is:

$$\begin{aligned} V_1 &=\sqrt{2} \pi \phi _m N \\ V_1&= \sqrt{2} \pi f B_m A N\\ \text{where,}\;\; \frac{V}{t} &=\text{constant} \end{aligned}$$

i.e. flux = constant ( to avoid over fluxing)

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Eddy current loss,} &P_e \propto V^2 \\ \text{and hysteresis loss,}&P_h \propto\frac{V^{1.6}}{f^{0.6}} \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{P_{e2}}{P_{e1}} &=\left ( \frac{V_2}{V_1} \right )^2=\left ( \frac{138}{230} \right )^2=0.36 \\ \text{or,} \;\; P_{e2} &= 0.36P_{e1}\;\;...(i)\\ \text{Also,} \;\;\frac{P_{h2}}{P_{e1}} &=\left ( \frac{V_2}{V_1} \right )^{1.6} \times \left ( \frac{f_1}{f_2} \right )^{0.6}\\ &=\left ( \frac{138}{230} \right )^{1.6} \times \left ( \frac{50}{30} \right )^{0.6} \\ &= (0.6)^{1.6} \times \frac{1}{(0.6)^{0.6}}=0.6\\ \therefore \;\; P_{h2} &=0.6P_{h1} \;\;...(ii) \end{aligned}$$

Given at 230V, 50Hz

$\text{Core loss}=P_{e1}+P_{h1}=1050W\;\;...(iii)$

At 138V, 30Hz,

$\text{Core loss}=P_{e2}+P_{h2}=500W$

or,   $0.36P_{e1}+0.6P_{h1}=500W\;\;...(iv)$

solving equation (iii) and (iv), we get

$P_{h1}=508W$ and $P_{e1}=542W$

Therefore, hysteresis and eddy current losses at 230V, 50Hz are 508W and 542W respectively.

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ee:2014:q44.question: For the given system, it is desired that the system be stable. The minimum value of $\alpha$ for this condition is ______.

ee:2014:q48.title: GATE EE 2014 | Set 1 | Question: 48
ee:2014:q48.question:
The dc current flowing in a circuit is measured by two ammeters, one PMMC
and another electrodynamometer type, connected in series. The PMMC meter
contains 100 turns in the coil, the flux density in the air gap is 0.2Wb/$m^2$, and
the area of the coil is 80 $mm^2$. The electrodynamometer ammeter has a change in

detailed_solution.markdown: For a PMMC ammeter, at equilibrim, we have : controlling torque ($T_c$)=Deflecting torque($T_d$) $$\begin{aligned} K\theta _1 &=GI \; \text{or}\; \theta _1=\frac{GI}{K}\\ where, \;\; G &= nBA\\ \therefore \; \theta _1 &= \frac{nBAI}{K} \end{aligned}$$ For an electrodynometer ammeter, at equilibrium, Controlling torque=Deflecting torque $$\begin{aligned} i.e. \;\; T_c &=T_d \; \text{or}\; K \theta _2=I^2 \frac{dM}{d\theta }\\ or, \;\; \theta _2 &= \frac{I^2}{K}\cdot \frac{dM}{d\theta }\;\;...(ii)\\ \end{aligned}$$ For the deflection in the two meter to be same, $$\begin{aligned} \theta _1 &=\theta _2\\ or, \;\; \frac{nBAI}{K} &= \frac{I^2}{K}\cdot \frac{dM}{d\theta }\\ or, \;\; nBA&=I\frac{dM}{d\theta }\\ or, \;\; I &=\frac{nBA}{\left ( \frac{dM}{d\theta } \right )} \end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned} Given, \;\; n&= \text{number of turns}=100\\ B&= 0.2 Wb/m^2\\ A&=80mm^2=80 \times 10^{-6}m^2\\ \text{and}\;\; \frac{dM}{d\theta }&=0.5 mH/rad\\ &=0.5 \times 10^{-3}H/rad \\ \end{aligned}$$ Putting the values in I, we get $$\begin{aligned} I &=\left ( \frac{100 \times 0.2 \times 80 \times 10^{-6}}{0.5 \times 10^{-3}} \right ) A\\ &= \frac{1.6}{0.5}=3.2A \end{aligned}$$ $\therefore$ Required value of current, $I=3.2Amp.$ Therefore, the correct answer is **3.2** (acceptable range: [3, 3.4]).

ee:2014:q54.question: Figure (i) shows the circuit diagram of a chopper. The switch S in the circuit in figure (i) is switched such that the voltage $v_D$ across the diode has the wave shape as shown in figure (ii). The capacitance C is large so that the voltage across it is constant. If switch S and the diode are ideal, the peak to peak ripple (in A) in the inductor current is ______

detailed_solution.markdown:
The circuit shown is a Buck chopper

$$\begin{aligned} V_0&=V_s\frac{T_{ON}}{T}\\ V_0&=100 \times \frac{0.05 \times 10^{-3}}{0.1 \times 10^{-3}}=50V \end{aligned}$$

The peak to peak ripple in the inductor current is

Therefore, the correct answer is **2.5** (acceptable range: [2.49, 2.51]).

ee:2014:q55.title: GATE EE 2014 | Set 1 | Question: 55
ee:2014:q55.question: The figure shows one period of the output voltage of an inverter. $\alpha$ should be chosen such that $60^{\circ} \lt \alpha \lt 90^{\circ}$. If rms value of the fundamental component is 50V, then $\alpha$ in degree is _____.

detailed_solution.markdown:
The output voltage $V_0$ can be reprresnted by fourier series as under:

$$\begin{aligned} V_0&=\sum_{n=1,3,5,...}^{\infty }a_n \cos n\omega t+b_n \sin n\omega t\\ \text{where, } a_n&=\frac{2}{T}\int_{0}^{T}f(t)\cos n\omega t \;d(\omega t) \\ b_n&=\frac{2}{T}\int_{0}^{T}f(t)\sin n\omega t \;d(\omega t) \\ a_n&=\frac{1}{\pi} [\int_{0}^{\alpha }100 \cos \omega t \;d(\omega t) +\int_{\alpha }^{180^{\circ}-\alpha }(-100) \cos \omega t \;d(\omega t) \\ &+ \int_{180^{\circ}-\alpha}^{180^{\circ} }100 \cos \omega t \;d(\omega t) +\int_{180^{\circ} }^{180^{\circ}+\alpha }(-100) \cos \omega t \;d(\omega t)\\ &+ \int_{180^{\circ}+\alpha}^{360^{\circ} -\alpha }100 \cos \omega t \;d(\omega t) +\int_{360^{\circ}-\alpha }^{360^{\circ} }(-100) \cos \omega t \;d(\omega t)]\\ a_n &=\frac{100}{\pi}[\sin \alpha - \sin (180^{\circ} -\alpha ) + \sin \alpha \\ &+\sin (180^{\circ}) -\sin (180^{\circ} -\alpha )\\ &- \sin (180^{\circ} +\alpha ) + \sin 180^{\circ}\\ &+ \sin (360^{\circ} -\alpha )- \sin (180^{\circ} +\alpha ) \\ &- \sin (360^{\circ} ) + \sin (360^{\circ} -\alpha )]\\ a_n &=0 \\ b_n&=\frac{1}{\pi} [\int_{0}^{\alpha }100 \sin \omega t \;d(\omega t) +\int_{\alpha }^{180^{\circ}-\alpha }(-100) \sin \omega t \;d(\omega t) \\ &+ \int_{180^{\circ}-\alpha}^{180^{\circ} }100 \sin \omega t \;d(\omega t) +\int_{180^{\circ} }^{180^{\circ}+\alpha }(-100) \sin \omega t \;d(\omega t)\\ &+ \int_{180^{\circ}+\alpha}^{360^{\circ} -\alpha }100 \sin \omega t \;d(\omega t) +\int_{360^{\circ}-\alpha }^{360^{\circ} }(-100) \sin \omega t \;d(\omega t)]\\ b_n &=\frac{100}{\pi}[-\cos \alpha +1+ \cos (180^{\circ} -\alpha ) - \cos \alpha \\ &-\cos (180^{\circ}) +\cos (180^{\circ} -\alpha )\\ &+ \cos (180^{\circ} +\alpha ) - \cos 180^{\circ}\\ &- \cos (360^{\circ} -\alpha )+ \cos (180^{\circ} +\alpha ) \\ &+ \cos (360^{\circ} ) - \cos (360^{\circ} -\alpha )]\\ b_n&=\frac{100}{\pi}[4-8 \cos \alpha ] =50\sqrt{2}\\ \cos \alpha &=0.22231=77.15^{\circ} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **77.25** (acceptable range: [76.5, 78]).
